summary:
Allwork.Space republishes a Reuters report on Silver Lake's potential take-private of Workday and what it signals about enterprise software valuations in the AI era. Workday shares jumped nearly 18% on Thursday after Reuters exclusively reported the acquisition talks, lifting its market value above $51 billion. Analysts and investors said a buyout at a substantial premium would suggest private equity retains confidence in enterprise software despite fears that AI code generation and app-building tools will erode demand for traditional software services, a sector hit hard this year.

Brian Mulberry of Zacks Investment Research argued that a Silver Lake deal at a premium would be among the strongest evidence yet that public markets have overshot in discounting traditional enterprise software because of AI. The piece also points to strong recent earnings from ServiceNow as evidence of staying power for vendors embedded in core functions such as HR, CRM and finance, where switching systems is costly and disruptive.

Market context cited: the S&P 500 Software & Services index is up roughly 25% quarter-to-date; SAP led a European software rally on Friday after U.S. peers including Salesforce, Adobe and ServiceNow gained between 1.9% and 4.5%. Morgan Stanley analysts said a Workday acquisition would validate the view that the company has a strong moat and a large opportunity to automate the back office, and that the report could inspire other potential acquirers, especially financial sponsors, to regain confidence in software investing, putting upward pressure on software stocks as short sellers retreat.

The item is financial and market-focused, covering HR and financial management software valuation rather than workplace operations, visitor management, desk booking, hybrid policy or facilities practice. Reporting by Rashika Singh in Bengaluru, edited by Shilpi Majumdar.
